column1: # Body inventory for the next transcriptions: recovered VA, the arm that installs
# it, and how many absolute operands it reads (each one is a published slot the
# arm must set before it installs). Measured with tools/verify_bodies.py and the
# reference sources; not a proof, a work list.
# name                          recovered VA  arm key                        slots
emissive_lerp_shim                 1001AF60  emissive_lerp_fix                    5#
# 0x10159CC4, 0x10159CC8, 0x10159CCC) and calls 0x1001AF20. Reading those
# addresses out of the original file gives bytes that decode as code, not as a
# the original's own fault) or the body was read from a different section layout
# until the operands are re-derived from the disassembly rather than assumed.
# EmissiveLerpFix - operands RESOLVED (2026-11-05). The five absolute operands are
# .bss scratch, not code: the IDB reads 0x10159CC0 as sixteen zero bytes, and
# image_offset used to map a .bss address into whatever section followed, which is
# why the same address appeared to hold code in the file. With that fixed (a bss
# address now maps to "not in the file"), the shim is a normal transcription: two
# scratch dwords, a float scale, a resume, and a call to the paired body at
# EmissiveLerpFix - operands resolved as addresses, but the *semantics* are not.
# IDB (session a4757382) gives the pair in full:
#   sub_1001AF60 (11 insns): save ECX/EDX to 0x10159CC0/0x10159CCC, pusha, call
#     sub_1001AF20, popa, reload ECX/EDX, cvtsi2ss xmm0,edx,
#     mulss xmm0,[0x10159CC4], jmp [0x10159CC8]
#   sub_1001AF20 (13 insns): pure scratch arithmetic on 0x10159CC0/0x10159CCC
#     with constants 0xC, 0xFFFFFE6B, 0x2ED, then retn
# Both 0x10159CC0 and 0x10159CC4 read as zero in the loaded image (.bss).
# The reference publish sets its two globals from the site: const = match-16,
# resume = match-12, i.e. *addresses*, while the shim's mulss/jmp consume absolute
# addresses directly. Direct-vs-pointer is exactly the difference between reading
# the game's float and reading a pointer as a float, so the transcription has to
# settle it from the original's bytes around the mulss (an explicit [reg] load
# would mean pointer) before any body is written.
